policy_text:
Ostrava-Lune Foundation, Halbrecht Early Inquiry Grants: eligibility rules (2027 cycle)
An application is approved only if it meets every rule below. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when an application is silent on a point.

R1. The project period, from start date to end date, may not exceed 39 weeks.
R2. Applications hosted by a teaching hospital may budget at most $5,000 for travel.
R3. The lead applicant must have received a doctorate no more than 6 years before 2027. This rule does not apply if the applicant has a documented Corran career break and the doctorate is at most 10 years old.
R4. The application must include a letter of support from the host. This rule does not apply if the host is a university, whose standing agreement with the foundation replaces the letter.
R5. If the type of host institution is not stated, treat the host as an independent institute.
R6. Research with human participants requires approval from the Mereth ethics board.
R7. If ethics approval is not mentioned, assume none was obtained.
R8. Equipment and travel together may not exceed $30,000.
R9. The host institution must be a university, a teaching hospital or a community laboratory.

case_sentences.sentence: Dr. Ilse Varnholt submitted application HEI-2079 to the Ostrava-Lune Foundation for the current cycle.
The ledger allocates exactly $10,000 for acquiring necessary equipment.
The financial summary requests a total disbursement of $60,000 from the foundation.
A graduate student drafted several sections of the project narrative.
The submission package lacks an endorsement letter from the host institution.
The accompanying budget justification employs a remarkably casual writing style.
Transportation and related transit expenses are set at $5,000.
No paperwork has been submitted to the Mereth ethics board by the applicant.
An academic institution located in the Vessel Bay region is named as the host.
The principal investigator was awarded their doctoral degree 3 years ago.
Combined expenditures for apparatus and transit total $15,000.
A submitted Corran career break form records a period of absence from active research.
The research design excludes any involvement of human participants.
Project activities are planned to commence on February 15, 2027.
The introductory letter expresses gratitude to two former mentors by name.
An appended document pledges that the research team will make all collected data publicly accessible.
Operations are projected to conclude on August 30, 2027.
The proposed timeline spans a duration of 28 weeks.

An application is approved only if it meets every rule below. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when an application is silent on a point.

R1. Requests above $50,000 must include a letter of support from the host.
R2. The lead applicant must have received a doctorate no more than 6 years before 2027, unless the applicant has a documented Corran career break and the doctorate is at most 10 years old.
R3. Every proposal must include an open data plan. This rule does not apply if the host is a teaching hospital bound by patient privacy rules.
R4. Applications hosted by a teaching hospital may budget at most $10,000 for travel.
R5. The total requested amount may not exceed $90,000. This rule does not apply if the host is a community laboratory and the request is at most $120,000.
R6. No project may begin before January 14, 2027.
R7. The host institution must be a university, a teaching hospital or a community laboratory.
R8. If an application does not mention a career break, assume the applicant took none.
R9. The project period, from start date to end date, may not exceed 39 weeks.
R10. Research with human participants requires approval from the Mereth ethics board.

An application is approved only if it meets every rule below. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when an application is silent on a point.

R1. Applications hosted by a teaching hospital may budget at most $5,000 for travel.
R2. The lead applicant must have received a doctorate no more than 8 years before 2027. This rule does not apply if the applicant has a documented Corran career break and the doctorate is at most 10 years old.
R3. The project period, from start date to end date, may not exceed 65 weeks.
R4. Requests above $50,000 must include a letter of support from the host.
R5. The application must include a letter of support from the host. This rule does not apply if the host is a university, whose standing agreement with the foundation replaces the letter.
R6. No project may begin before February 8, 2027.
R7. If an application does not mention a career break, assume the applicant took none.
R8. Equipment and travel together may not exceed $30,000.
R9. Research with human participants requires approval from the Mereth ethics board.

R9. If the site tier is not recorded, treat the site as tier B.

A participant is enrolled (approved) only if every criterion below is met. Criteria marked as defaults say what to assume when the screening record is silent on a point.

R1. Screening must take place on or after the consent date and no more than 14 days after it.
R2. The Halden composite score (PRX-7 level in ng/mL plus ten times the Kelman index) may not exceed 300.
R3. Participants must be between 35 and 75 years old inclusive.
R4. Creatinine clearance must be at least 75 mL/min, unless the participant is enrolled at a tier A Halvard site and creatinine clearance is at least 60 mL/min.
R5. Participants taking an anticoagulant are excluded, unless they enroll at a tier A Halvard site, where coagulation is monitored weekly.
R6. At least 8 weeks must have passed since the last systemic therapy.
R7. Participants on an anticoagulant must have no history of major bleeding.
R8. Participants on an anticoagulant must have a resting heart rate of at most 85 beats per minute.
R9. If the record does not mention prior celvorex exposure, assume there was none.
R10. Participants previously exposed to celvorex are excluded.
R11. If the record does not mention bleeding, assume no history of major bleeding.

case_sentences.sentence: Candidate evaluation documentation for clinical trial VX-118 references prospective subject number 1561.
The individual traveled a distance of two hours to arrive at the investigative center.
Discontinuation of prior systemic treatment occurred twelve weeks prior to the screening evaluation.
The baseline screening assessment was conducted on February 8, 2027.
Assessment of renal clearance demonstrated a creatinine clearance value of 120 mL/min.
Analysis from the central laboratory indicated a PRX-7 concentration of 150 ng/mL.
Radiological evaluation established a Kelman index measurement of 4.
Current medication regimen excludes the use of any anticoagulant therapy.
Medical history documentation indicates past administration of celvorex.
The resting pulse rate recorded during the physical examination was 105 beats per minute.
The subject's chronological age is documented as 60 years.
Review of the medical background reveals no prior episodes of major hemorrhage.
Language assistance services were made available upon arrival but were declined.
The participant signed the informed consent document on February 4, 2027.
The screening procedures were performed 4 days following the execution of the consent form.
Calculation of the Halden composite score yielded a total of 190 points.
Outside of clinical visits, the individual is employed professionally as a piano technician.
The evaluation took place at a designated tier A Halvard clinical facility.
Initial proceedings experienced a brief thirty-minute delay due to an administrative scheduling conflict.

policy_text:
Protocol VX-118 (celvorex in Tarrant fibrosis): enrollment criteria
A participant is enrolled (approved) only if every criterion below is met. Criteria marked as defaults say what to assume when the screening record is silent on a point.

R1. At least 4 weeks must have passed since the last systemic therapy.
R2. Participants on an anticoagulant must have no history of major bleeding.
R3. The PRX-7 serum level must be at least 200 ng/mL, unless the Kelman index is 8 or higher.
R4. If the site tier is not recorded, treat the site as tier B.
R5. If the record does not mention anticoagulants, assume the participant takes none.
R6. Participants must be between 35 and 65 years old inclusive.
R7. Screening must take place on or after the consent date and no more than 21 days after it.
R8. Creatinine clearance must be at least 75 mL/min, unless the participant is enrolled at a tier A Halvard site and creatinine clearance is at least 60 mL/min.
R9. Participants on an anticoagulant must have a resting heart rate of at most 85 beats per minute.
R10. The Halden composite score (PRX-7 level in ng/mL plus ten times the Kelman index) may not exceed 400.
R11. Participants aged 60 or older need a creatinine clearance of at least 90 mL/min.
R12. Tier C Halvard sites may only enroll participants aged 55 or younger.

A participant is enrolled (approved) only if every criterion below is met. Criteria marked as defaults say what to assume when the screening record is silent on a point.

R1. Tier C Halvard sites may only enroll participants aged 55 or younger.
R2. Participants on an anticoagulant must have no history of major bleeding.
R3. Participants previously exposed to celvorex are excluded.
R4. If the record does not mention bleeding, assume no history of major bleeding.
R5. Participants aged 70 or older need a creatinine clearance of at least 90 mL/min.
R6. Creatinine clearance must be at least 60 mL/min, unless the participant is enrolled at a tier A Halvard site and creatinine clearance is at least 45 mL/min.
R7. Screening must take place on or after the consent date and no more than 14 days after it.
R8. Participants taking an anticoagulant are excluded, unless they enroll at a tier A Halvard site, where coagulation is monitored weekly.
R9. Participants on an anticoagulant must have a resting heart rate of at most 85 beats per minute.

The Kelman fibrosis index may not exceed 8.
Participants on an anticoagulant must have no history of major bleeding.
Participants aged 70 or older need a creatinine clearance of at least 105 mL/min.
Screening must take place on or after the consent date and no more than 21 days after it.
Creatinine clearance must be at least 60 mL/min. This rule does not apply if the participant is enrolled at a tier A Halvard site and creatinine clearance is at least 45 mL/min.
The PRX-7 serum level must be at least 150 ng/mL, unless the Kelman index is 8 or higher.

policy_text:
Twelfth Symposium on Quorian Methods (SQM 2027): submission and review policy
A submission is admitted to review with its assigned reviewer (approved) only if it meets every rule below. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the submission record is silent on a point.

R1. The main text and references together may not exceed 11 pages.
R2. Supplementary material may not exceed 50 MB. This rule does not apply if the paper is in the Applied Quorian track, which allows up to 100 MB.
R3. Applied Quorian track papers may use at most 3 pages of references.
R4. Submissions must be uploaded no later than April 17, 2027, unless the chairs granted an extension and the paper was uploaded by April 21, 2027.
R5. The assigned reviewer may not work at the same institution as any author, unless the paper is in the Position Paper track, which is reviewed openly by the whole committee.
R6. The assigned reviewer may not have co-authored a paper with any author within 365 days before the submission date.
R7. Papers reporting studies with human participants must include an ethics statement. This rule does not apply if the paper is in the Position Paper track.
R8. Any supplementary material must be anonymized.
R9. If the record does not say whether supplementary material is anonymized, treat it as not anonymized.
R10. Papers uploaded under a deadline extension may not exceed 7 pages of main text.
R11. If the record does not mention an ethics statement, assume there is none.

A submission is admitted to review with its assigned reviewer (approved) only if it meets every rule below. Rules marked as defaults say what to assume when the submission record is silent on a point.

R1. The main text and references together may not exceed 12 pages.
R2. Any supplementary material must be anonymized.
R3. Papers reporting studies with human participants must include an ethics statement. This rule does not apply if the paper is in the Position Paper track.
R4. Position papers may list at most 3 authors.
R5. Applied Quorian track papers may use at most 3 pages of references.
R6. If the record does not mention a license for supplementary artifacts, assume they carry none.
R7. The manuscript must be anonymized, unless it is submitted to the Position Paper track, which is reviewed with author names visible.
R8. If the record does not say whether supplementary material is anonymized, treat it as not anonymized.
R9. Any supplementary artifacts must be released under an open license.
R10. The assigned reviewer may not have co-authored a paper with any author within 730 days before the submission date.
